title: Omni Documents are the residual category that keeps non-Primitive activity out of the Primitive tree
content:
A.6.1.1.6.3 defines the Omni Documents as covering "Pattern's strategic intent and operational processes relating to infrastructure inherited from Sky Core, activities unrelated to Sky Primitives, or activities spanning multiple Sky Primitives."

The category solves a structural problem. An Artifact organized strictly by Primitive has nowhere to put three real classes of content: inherited infrastructure that belongs to no single Primitive, genuine activity that no Primitive models, and cross-cutting processes that would otherwise have to be duplicated under several Primitives or arbitrarily assigned to one. Without a residual bucket, such content either gets forced into the nearest Primitive — corrupting the taxonomy — or goes undocumented.

The first entry demonstrates the discipline. A.6.1.1.6.3.1 is titled "Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive" and immediately redirects: "The governance process for updating the Pattern Artifact is specified in the Root Edit Primitive above." The residual section is explicitly defined by *exclusion* from the Primitive that owns the topic, rather than being allowed to accumulate a competing account of it.

What lands there is correspondingly thin and infrastructural — for example that "Pattern uses the Sky Forum for governance-related discussion" under the "Pattern Prime" category (A.6.1.1.6.3.1.1), the venue every other process in the Artifact assumes without defining.
description: They hold strategic intent and processes for infrastructure inherited from Sky Core, activity unrelated to any Sky Primitive, and activity spanning several Primitives at once.
